$comment: Phase 22 acceptance definition derived from architecture/phase-22-mobile-platform.md, the phase contract, platform-core/device/offline/observability/client-platform modules and the cited platform suites. Client classification, offline and trust models are tested libraries; no native release or server re-authorization boundary is inferred.

ownership.note: Phase 22 owns client capability profiles, offline queue semantics, push delivery records and client observability. Domain surfaces, authorization and web behaviour remain owned by consuming or adjacent phases.

areas.area: Mobile platform profiles classify devices and targets
areas.requirement: Real device families, touch capability, responsive breakpoints, color scheme and platform targets are classified into the declared vocabulary; unknown targets fail closed.

evidence.contains: maps real device UA strings into the P22 vocabulary

areas.area: Client launch, deep links, routes and API requests are typed
areas.requirement: Launch sources, deep links, known navigation routes and authenticated API request shapes are represented and invalid route/input values are rejected.

evidence.contains: creates launch context from deep link with payload

areas.area: Offline synchronization and resource constraints are explicit
areas.requirement: Offline operations and cache entries have state, expiry and eviction rules, while weak bandwidth and low power cause constrained sync behaviour.

areas.area: Device trust and device capabilities are fail-closed
areas.requirement: Compromised or debug devices are not trusted, minimum requirements and sensitive permissions are evaluated explicitly, and biometric outcomes are represented.

evidence.contains: returns unknown when debug mode detected

areas.area: Client telemetry, audit and compatibility records are privacy-aware
areas.requirement: Telemetry is anonymized, client audit events are typed, AI interactions are recorded and version compatibility/OTA state is evaluable.

evidence.contains: compatible when app version meets minimum

areas.area: Server re-authorization and native delivery remain unwired
areas.requirement: Queued actions must be re-authorized server-side and a native delivery/release boundary must consume the client contracts; current evidence is client-library testing only.
